sources.title: Tagged interview note preserving three-table SQL/subquery prompt

claims.text: The source preserves a generic three-table association query with subquery implementation request, but no concrete schema, fields, business filter or target output.

Under the declared students/courses/scores reference exercise, the exact SQL matches an independent relational oracle for above-global-average student aggregates and distinct course counts across explicit and 12,000 seeded random fixtures.

validation.command: SQLite execution of exact SQL candidate against independent Python relational oracle
validation.reported_stdout: PASS duplicate-course-facts=oracle empty=covered randomized-fixtures=12000 aggregate-threshold=exact distinct-course-count=exact

boundary_tests.case: duplicate facts for the same student/course plus another course
boundary_tests.expected: AVG consumes every valid fact row while COUNT(DISTINCT course_id) counts course identities once
exact rows, student averages, strict global-average threshold and distinct course count match independent Python oracle

findings: The source preserves only a three-table association/subquery implementation prompt and does not preserve schema, fields or one business result; the candidate explicitly declares its students/courses/scores example as a reference exercise.

The reference query has a coherent result grain of one student per row, uses both three-table join relationships, computes student aggregates in the outer query and a scalar global-score aggregate in the subquery.
The answer correctly distinguishes pre-aggregation WHERE semantics from aggregate HAVING semantics and warns against using DISTINCT score to hide data-model duplication.

Independent randomized differential testing over 12,000 fixtures matches an oracle for strict above-global-average selection, aggregate values and distinct course counts, including duplicate fact rows and empty scores.

The candidate explicitly scopes INNER JOIN no-score behavior, duplicate-fact semantics, NULL/empty behavior and execution-plan/index validation as contract or operational concerns rather than preserved source facts.
